transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for fitting me in. 

Um... well, I guess what brings me in is... I'm just having a little trouble—well, maybe more than a little—keeping my mind on a task long enough to actually finish it anymore. It's probably just me getting older or maybe a bit of stress, but it's happening even when the work is really important. 

Like, I do computer support, and I'll sit down to start tracing a client's network problem, and... I don't know, ten minutes later I'll realize I've just reread the exact same log entries three times. And I still don't even know what they say. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly, a guy my age struggling with something so basic. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining
Did you have trouble paying attention as a child?

Oh, um... as a child? Well, I guess... I mean, I was a good kid, mostly. I didn't mean to cause any trouble. But, um... my mother actually still jokes about it sometimes. She says my grade school report cards always said I was bright, which was nice of the teachers to say, but... they also usually mentioned that I had a hard time staying in my seat. 

And, um, I guess I would sometimes blurt out answers before the teacher finished asking the question. I just got so eager, you know? And I'd lose my homework... even when I had actually done it. It was just so frustrating to know I did the work and then couldn't find it. 

But I wasn't trying to be difficult or anything! I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad kid. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have these concentration problems been present pretty much your whole adult life?

Um, my whole adult life? Well... I guess maybe? I mean, I've always managed to hold down a job and take care of things, so I don't want to make it sound like I've been completely non-functional or anything. I've always tried really hard to do good work.

But... yeah, I suppose if I really think about it, I've always had to put in a lot of extra hours just to keep up. Like, I'd stay late at the office when everyone else went home, just because it was quieter and I could finally focus. I always just thought I was a hard worker, you know? Or maybe just a little scatterbrained sometimes. 

It's only recently that it feels like... like I just can't push through it the way I used to. The extra effort just isn't working anymore. But I've always gotten by before! I hope that makes sense. Is that normal for people to experience?
Have you been feeling depressed lately?

Depressed? Oh, no, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I have a lot to be thankful for, really. I've got a good job, and I'm healthy... mostly. 

I mean, sure, it gets a little frustrating when I can't seem to get my work done, like I mentioned. It's a bit of a bummer to feel like you're falling behind, but I don't think I'm depressed. I still enjoy my hobbies when I can get around to them, and I'm not, you know, sad all the time or anything like that. 

I just want to be able to do my job right, you know? I want to be reliable. So, no, not depressed. I hope that's a good thing, right? I'm just trying to figure out why my brain feels so... scattered lately.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even about everyday things?

Worrying? Oh, um... no, not really. I wouldn't call myself a worrier. I mean, I want to do a good job, obviously. In my line of work—doing computer support—people are really relying on you to fix their issues, so I always want to make sure I'm doing things right and keeping everyone happy. 

But I don't sit around agonizing over everyday things. I try to stay pretty positive! I mean, sure, it gets a little stressful if I misplace a work ticket or fall behind on my queue, but I don't think I have an anxiety problem or anything like that. I just want to be helpful and do my best. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I just wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, overly anxious. I'm usually a pretty upbeat guy!
Have you been forgetting appointments or conversations more than you used to?

Um, forgetting things? Well... I mean, everybody forgets things sometimes, right? Especially when you get to be my age. It's not like I'm completely losing my mind or anything! I try really hard to keep track of everything. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, there have been a few little slip-ups lately. Just silly things, really! Like... I might forget to return a client's call right away, or... or I'll realize I forgot to pay the cloud backup bill on time. And the other day, I was volunteering to teach this computer class, and I completely forgot to bring the right adapter. 

It's just embarrassing, you know? I hate letting people down. I always end up spending the next day just apologizing to everyone and trying to fix whatever I messed up. I just want to be reliable for people. I hope you don't think I'm just careless or irresponsible. I really do try my best! Does that sound like a normal amount of forgetting to you?
Have these memory and focus problems gotten noticeably worse over the past year or two compared with how you were before?

Well, um... I guess you could say it's been a bit more noticeable lately. But, you know, it's not like I've always been this scattered! I used to be really on top of things, I promise. 

It's just... well, about a year and ten months ago, I had a little... setback. I actually, um, I lost my job. I mean, they let me go. It wasn't because I'm a bad worker! It's just that, at my old job, I had all these systems in place, you know? Checklists, reminders, a whole routine that really kept me on track. And since then, without all that structure... I guess things have just been a lot harder to manage. 

It's been causing some pretty serious trouble for me, honestly. But I'm trying really hard to get back into a good groove! I just need to find a new system that works for me. That makes sense, right? It's normal to struggle a bit when you lose your routine? I just don't want you to think I'm making excuses.
Around the time these problems got worse, did you have a head injury?

A head injury? Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely nothing like that! I haven't hit my head or been in any accidents or anything. 

I've always been pretty careful, honestly. I know how important it is to stay safe and healthy, especially when you're trying to get back into the workforce. So, no, no concussions or anything scary like that. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, it's better that it's not a head injury, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so we can figure this out. I'm really trying to be helpful!
Have you started needing help with everyday tasks like managing bills, medications, or keeping track of appointments?

Needing help? Oh, um... no, no, definitely not. I mean, I know I just said I missed that one cloud backup bill, but I still handle all of that myself! I don't need anyone to actually do it for me or anything like that. 

I'm completely independent with my everyday stuff. Medications, paying the
Has anyone close to you noticed that your memory or thinking has gotten worse?

Oh, um, noticed my memory getting worse? No, no, I don't think so. I mean, my wife sometimes teases me about being a little scatterbrained, but that's just... that's just normal marriage stuff, right? 

She hasn't sat me down and said she's worried about my thinking or anything serious like that. I really try to make sure my little slip-ups don't affect anyone else. I wouldn't want to be a burden or have people worrying about me. 

So, no, nobody has said anything about a decline. That means I'm still doing okay, wouldn't you say? I'm really trying to keep it all together.
Before the past couple of years, did you ever have this kind of trouble with your memory?

Trouble with my memory before? Oh, no, absolutely not. I've always been really sharp, actually. I mean, working in IT, you kind of have to be, right? Remembering all those different system configurations and troubleshooting steps... I was always on top of it. 

I was always the guy people came to when they couldn't figure something out. So, no, my memory has always been really solid up until recently. 

It's just this recent stretch that's been a little... tricky. But before that, I was completely fine. That's a good sign, though, isn't it? That it's just a recent thing and not something I've always struggled with? I really hope so. I just want to get back to being the reliable guy I've always been.
Were you let go from your last job because your memory or thinking problems were affecting your work?

Let go? Oh, no, no. I wasn't fired or anything like that. I mean, they didn't push me out because of my memory. 

I just... I decided to step away. It was a mutual thing, really. The IT field is just so fast-paced, you know? Always changing. And I figured it was a good time to maybe look for something a little different, maybe a bit less stressful. 

But it wasn't because I couldn't do the work or because they thought I was slipping. I made sure to leave on good terms. I wouldn't want anyone to think I couldn't handle my job. That's not the case at all, right? I mean, stepping away on your own terms is a completely normal thing to do at my age, isn't it?
When someone tells you something important, do you usually remember it later if you were paying full attention at the time?

Oh, yes, absolutely. If I'm really focused and paying full attention, I definitely remember important things. I mean, I'm a good listener, especially when it matters. 

Sometimes, if there's a lot going on, you know, background noise or if someone catches me right in the middle of a complicated task, I might need them to repeat it. But that happens to everyone, right? It's just a matter of being fully present in the moment. 

If I'm dialed in, the information sticks. I wouldn't want you to think I just let important things slip through the cracks. That would be terrible. So, yes, as long as I'm paying attention, my memory for that kind of stuff is perfectly fine. That's the normal way it works for most people, isn't it?
